records.text: Paper card. Question: How do Ti-Mo-Zr-Ta-Si alloys behave in terms of microstructure, mechanical properties, and biocompatibility for potential implant applications?. System: Ti-Mo-Zr-Ta-Si alloys with varying silicon content (0.5, 0.75, 1 wt.%). Processing: Vacuum Arc Remelting with melting power of min. 55 kVA, melting current of min. 650 A, and vacuum level of 4.5 × 10−3 mbar. Test conditions: In vitro cytocompatibility tests with fibroblasts and osteoblasts, and in vivo biocompatibility assessment in rabbits for 60 days. Findings: Hardness and modulus of elasticity increased with silicon content; Ti-Mo-Zr-Ta-Si materials showed no toxic interactions with cells; Cell viability increased with higher silicon content; Osseointegration was promoted in titanium alloys containing Mo, Zr, Ta, and Si; High expression of OPN, MMP2, and MMP9 in osteoprogenitor cells, osteoblasts, and osteocytes. Mechanism: The addition of silicon to the Ti-Mo-Zr-Ta system favored the presence of the β phase, leading to increased hardness and modulus of elasticity. Quote: "the hardness and the modulus of elasticity increased"
